previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and multiple airway reconstructions was admitted for persistent tracheostomy site pain and productive cough with green sputum. She had ongoing symptoms since a recent hospitalization where Pseudomonas aeruginosa was cultured but deemed colonizing. This admission, with continued pain and no improvement, the infection was re-evaluated as active bacterial tracheitis. A chest X-ray showed no pulmonary abnormalities, and endoscopic evaluation confirmed mild tracheal inflammation. She was treated with intravenous and then oral ciprofloxacin, with improvement in pain and systemic symptoms. Dizziness was attributed to chronic issues and improved with IV fluids. She remained stable, maintained oxygenation, and was discharged home on a full course of oral antibiotics with follow-up arranged with ENT and her primary care provider.
